transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what’s been troubling you or what brings you in today?

Hi. Um, well, I'm here because for the last couple of years, I just feel low all the time. It's like... even when I'm at work, or at church, or around people I really care about, there's just this heavy, empty feeling. It just doesn't really lift.
Before these feelings started, did you go through any major life changes, losses, or stressful events that might have triggered this?

Well, I guess the biggest thing was when I had to stop going to school. This has been going on for about two years and four months now, which is right around the time I had to drop my community-college classes. I just couldn't afford it anymore, and with my work schedule, I couldn't make it fit. So, yeah, I'd say that's when it all started.
Have there been times when you felt unusually high, overly energetic, or irritable, where you didn’t feel like you needed much sleep or felt like you could take on a lot more than usual?

No, um... I haven't really had anything like that. I don't think I've ever felt unusually high or, you know, overly energetic. It's pretty much just been that same heavy, low feeling I mentioned. I definitely haven't had times where I didn't need sleep or felt like I could take on a bunch of extra stuff.
Has the low feeling you mentioned been present most of the day, nearly every day, for the entire two-year period?

Yes, it really has. I mean, pretty much every single day. There might be a few days here and there where it's not quite as bad, but overall, it's just... there. Most of the day, every day, for the whole time since I left school.
Have you noticed a loss of interest or pleasure in activities that you used to enjoy, like hobbies, work, or spending time with friends and family?

Yes, definitely. I used to do a lot of things... I played basketball, went to dance nights, and I volunteered mentoring kids in STEM at my church. I really cared about all of that, but I've mostly stopped showing up to everything. I just don't have the interest anymore. And it's affecting my job as an inspector, too. I've actually gotten written warnings at work lately because I've been missing shifts and turning in my inspection documentation late. I just can't seem to get myself to care or do what I'm supposed to do.
Over the past couple of years, have you noticed any changes in your appetite or weight—like eating a lot more or less than usual, or gaining or losing weight without trying?

Yeah, I have noticed that. Most days I either skip eating until my shift is almost over, mostly just because nothing really sounds good to me. Or I'll end up grabbing snacks from the vending machine late in the day because I'm just too drained to do anything else. Because of that, my weight has definitely been going up and down. It changes enough that my work pants will actually fit differently from month to month.
Have you felt fatigued or had a loss of energy nearly every day for the past two years?

Yes, pretty much every day. I just feel so drained. Even small stuff like filling out my inspection logs at work, or driving to the basketball court, or just washing my hair... it feels like it takes way more energy than I actually have. And even when I try to rest on my days off, it doesn't really refill me. I still wake up feeling exhausted.
Have you often felt worthless or guilty, maybe blaming yourself for things even when it wasn't really your fault?

No, I don't think so. I mean, I feel bad about missing work and letting down the kids I used to mentor, but I don't really sit around feeling worthless or like everything is my fault. I'm just... tired and not interested in things.
Have you found it hard to focus, make decisions, or think clearly most days over the past two years?

No, I haven't really noticed any problems with that. I mean, I'm tired all the time, but when I actually have to do my job and inspect things, I can still focus on it. And making decisions hasn't been an issue either. I just don't have the energy to do much, but my thinking feels fine.
Have you ever felt so slowed down that even simple tasks took a lot longer, or the opposite—like you couldn't sit still or kept fidgeting a lot?

No, not really. I mean, I know I said earlier that things take a lot of energy to do, but I don't think I'm actually moving slower than normal. And I definitely don't get restless or fidgety. Physically, I feel like I move at a normal pace... I just feel exhausted while I'm doing it.

Before this two-year period of feeling low, did you have any periods lasting at least a few weeks where you felt significantly depressed, and were there times in your life when you were completely free of these feelings for at least two months?

No, I don't think so. I mean, it's just been this... constant low for the last two years. I don't remember any time before that where I felt really depressed for weeks at a time. And since this started, I haven't had any breaks from it. It hasn't gone away for two months, or even a few weeks. It's just always there.
Have you ever had a period of time where you felt unusually excited, agitated, or overly energetic for several days or more, where it was different from your usual self?

No, I've never felt like that. I don't get excited or overly energetic at all. It's really just been this same tired, low feeling the whole time. I've never had a few days where I felt agitated or like I had too much energy.
